assumptions: the substrate executed the check as written (ASM-SUBSTRATE-INTEGRITY)
attrs.evidence: Implemented for ONE verifier and declared as policy for the rest. scripts/check-integration.mjs returns 0 PASS, 1 FAIL, 2 NOT_STATED; --report-only never emits a PASS verdict; make-invariant-review-bundle.sh refuses 2 exactly as it refuses 1. THE UNIVERSAL FORM OF THIS CLAIM WAS SHIPPED PROVED AT INV-R9.3 AND WAS FALSE OF THIS ARTIFACT: GPT-5.6 reproduced check-publication-identity.mjs printing `walk is NOT stated` at exit 0 and check-lineage.mjs printing `draft count is NOT stated` at exit 0. Its own gap said so — `one gate has three outcomes and the other fifteen have two` — and a gap paragraph was allowed to narrow a universal statement after the status had been granted. GPT-5.6 also ruled that mechanically converting every gate is the WRONG repair: a checker total over its declared inputs needs no NOT_STATED, and the missing object is a census of which gates are partial over their environment.
attrs.gap: NO CENSUS EXISTS. Until one does, nothing here says which of the sixteen gates OUGHT to be three-valued, so the policy cannot be enforced and is DECLARED for exactly that reason. The exact-scope result is FAC-INTEGRATION-NOT-STATED-NONPASSING and it is the only thing this artifact has PROVED about the subject.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6’s INV-R9.2 audit §4. It is the consumer-boundary form of FAC-RESIDUAL-TRUST-UNGATED, which INV-R9.2 opened at the argument boundary: honest disclosure of an unproved premise is not refusal to consume the result.
attrs.review_focus: A census of partial-versus-total gates is the next object. Is `partial over its execution environment` decidable from a gate’s inputs, or does each gate have to declare it?
attrs.statement: FACTORY DESIGN RULE: a required verifier result that is not established may not be consumed as PASS. Where a checker is partial over its execution environment, NOT STATED is a third outcome distinct from PASS and FAIL, and a promotion may consume only PASS.
